core_reasoning_2:
\section*{Claim}
For all $U,V\in SU(2)$,
\[
\operatorname{tr}U\,\operatorname{tr}V=\operatorname{tr}(UV)+\operatorname{tr}(UV^\dagger).
\]
\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}&\quad U,V\in SU(2),\quad V^\dagger=V^{-1},\quad \det V=1.\\
\text{(P2)}&\quad \text{For every }2\times2\text{ matrix }A,\quad A^2-(\operatorname{tr}A)A+(\det A)I=0.\\
\text{(P3)}&\quad \operatorname{tr}(A+B)=\operatorname{tr}A+\operatorname{tr}B,
\quad \operatorname{tr}(cA)=c\operatorname{tr}A,
\quad \operatorname{tr}(UI)=\operatorname{tr}U.
\end{aligned}
\]
\section*{Derivation}
\begin{align}
V^2-(\operatorname{tr}V)V+I&=0 &&\text{by (P1) and (P2)}\\
\bigl(V^2-(\operatorname{tr}V)V+I\bigr)V^{-1}&=0\cdot V^{-1} &&\text{right-multiply by }V^{-1}\\
V-(\operatorname{tr}V)I+V^{-1}&=0 &&\text{since }VV^{-1}=I\\
V+V^\dagger&=(\operatorname{tr}V)I &&\text{by (P1)}\\
U(V+V^\dagger)&=U(\operatorname{tr}V)I &&\text{left-multiply by }U\\
UV+UV^\dagger&=(\operatorname{tr}V)U &&\text{distributivity}\\
\operatorname{tr}(UV)+\operatorname{tr}(UV^\dagger)&=\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{tr}V)U) &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=(\operatorname{tr}V)(\operatorname{tr}U) &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\operatorname{tr}U\,\operatorname{tr}V &&\text{commutativity of scalar multiplication}.
\end{align}
\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{tr}U\,\operatorname{tr}V=\operatorname{tr}(UV)+\operatorname{tr}(UV^\dagger)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_4:
\section*{Claim}
For the finite-$N$ special-unitary one-matrix model
\[
Z=\int DU\exp\left(\frac{N}{\lambda}(\operatorname{tr}U^\dagger+\operatorname{tr}U)\right),
\]
with normalized trace $\operatorname{Tr}A:=N^{-1}\operatorname{tr}A$, the double-trace loop equation for $n>0$ is
\[
\left\langle \frac{m}{N^2}\operatorname{Tr}U^{n+m}+\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}\operatorname{Tr}U^r\operatorname{Tr}U^{n-r}\operatorname{Tr}U^m+\frac1\lambda\operatorname{Tr}U^m(\operatorname{Tr}U^{n+1}-\operatorname{Tr}U^{n-1})\right\rangle
=\left\langle \frac{m+n}{N^2}\operatorname{Tr}U^n\operatorname{Tr}U^m+\frac1\lambda\operatorname{Tr}U^n\operatorname{Tr}U^m(\operatorname{Tr}U-\operatorname{Tr}U^\dagger)\right\rangle .
\]
\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}&\quad \langle F(U)\rangle:=Z^{-1}\int DU\,F(U)\exp\left(\frac{N}{\lambda}(\operatorname{tr}U^\dagger+\operatorname{tr}U)\right).\\
\text{(P2)}&\quad \operatorname{Tr}A:=N^{-1}\operatorname{tr}A.\\
\text{(P3)}&\quad \int DU\,\delta_\epsilon\left((U^n)_{ab}\operatorname{Tr}U^m\exp\left(\frac{N}{\lambda}(\operatorname{tr}U^\dagger+\operatorname{tr}U)\right)\right)=0,\\
&\quad \text{for every traceless Hermitian }\epsilon\text{ and every }n>0.\\
\text{(P4)}&\quad \delta_\epsilon(U^n)_{ab}=i\epsilon_{cd}\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}(U^r)_{ac}(U^{n-r})_{db}.\\
\text{(P5)}&\quad \delta_\epsilon\operatorname{Tr}U^m=i\epsilon_{cd}\frac{m}{N}(U^m)_{dc}.\\
\text{(P6)}&\quad \delta_\epsilon\exp\left(\frac{N}{\lambda}(\operatorname{tr}U^\dagger+\operatorname{tr}U)\right)
=i\epsilon_{cd}\frac{N}{\lambda}(U_{dc}-U^\dagger_{dc})\exp\left(\frac{N}{\lambda}(\operatorname{tr}U^\dagger+\operatorname{tr}U)\right).\\
\text{(P7)}&\quad \epsilon_{cd}X_{dc}=0\text{ for all traceless Hermitian }\epsilon\quad\Longrightarrow\quad X_{dc}=N^{-1}\delta_{dc}X_{ff}.\\
\text{(P8)}&\quad N^{-2}\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}\,(U^p)_{ab}(U^q)_{dc}=N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}U^{p+q}.\\
\text{(P9)}&\quad N^{-2}\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}\,(U^p)_{ac}(U^q)_{db}=\operatorname{Tr}U^p\operatorname{Tr}U^q.\\
\text{(P10)}&\quad N^{-2}\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}\delta_{dc}(U^p)_{ab}=N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}U^p.
\end{aligned}
\]
\section*{Derivation}
Expanding (P3) by the product rule and using (P4)--(P6) gives
\begin{align}
0&=i\epsilon_{cd}\left\langle
\frac{m}{N}(U^n)_{ab}(U^m)_{dc}
+\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}(U^r)_{ac}(U^{n-r})_{db}\operatorname{Tr}U^m
+\frac{N}{\lambda}(U^n)_{ab}\operatorname{Tr}U^m(U_{dc}-U^\dagger_{dc})
\right\rangle .
\end{align}
Define the bracketed tensor by $X_{dc,ab}$. Since $\epsilon$ is arbitrary and traceless, (P7) implies
\begin{align}
\langle X_{dc,ab}\rangle&=N^{-1}\delta_{dc}\langle X_{ff,ab}\rangle &&\text{by (P7)}\\
&=\delta_{dc}\left\langle
\frac{m}{N}(U^n)_{ab}\operatorname{Tr}U^m
+\frac{n}{N}(U^n)_{ab}\operatorname{Tr}U^m
+\frac{N}{\lambda}(U^n)_{ab}\operatorname{Tr}U^m(\operatorname{Tr}U-\operatorname{Tr}U^\dagger)
\right\rangle &&\text{take }X_{ff,ab}\text{ and use (P2)}.
\end{align}
Contract both sides with $N^{-2}\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}$. The contracted left-hand side is
\begin{align}
N^{-2}\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}\langle X_{dc,ab}\rangle
&=\left\langle
\frac{m}{N}\left(N^{-2}\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}(U^n)_{ab}(U^m)_{dc}\right)\right.\\
&\quad\left.+\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}\left(N^{-2}\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}(U^r)_{ac}(U^{n-r})_{db}\right)\operatorname{Tr}U^m\right.\\
&\quad\left.+\frac{N}{\lambda}\operatorname{Tr}U^m\left(N^{-2}\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}(U^n)_{ab}(U_{dc}-U^\dagger_{dc})\right)
\right\rangle &&\text{substitute }X_{dc,ab}\\
&=\left\langle
\frac{m}{N^2}\operatorname{Tr}U^{n+m}
+\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}\operatorname{Tr}U^r\operatorname{Tr}U^{n-r}\operatorname{Tr}U^m
+\frac1\lambda\operatorname{Tr}U^m(\operatorname{Tr}U^{n+1}-\operatorname{Tr}U^{n-1})
\right\rangle &&\text{by (P1), (P2), (P8), and (P9)}.
\end{align}
The contracted right-hand side is
\begin{align}
&N^{-2}\delta_{ac}\delta_{bd}\delta_{dc}\left\langle
\frac{m}{N}(U^n)_{ab}\operatorname{Tr}U^m
+\frac{n}{N}(U^n)_{ab}\operatorname{Tr}U^m
+\frac{N}{\lambda}(U^n)_{ab}\operatorname{Tr}U^m(\operatorname{Tr}U-\operatorname{Tr}U^\dagger)
\right\rangle\\
&=\left\langle
\frac{m}{N^2}\operatorname{Tr}U^n\operatorname{Tr}U^m
+\frac{n}{N^2}\operatorname{Tr}U^n\operatorname{Tr}U^m
+\frac1\lambda\operatorname{Tr}U^n\operatorname{Tr}U^m(\operatorname{Tr}U-\operatorname{Tr}U^\dagger)
\right\rangle &&\text{by (P10)}\\
&=\left\langle
\frac{m+n}{N^2}\operatorname{Tr}U^n\operatorname{Tr}U^m
+\frac1\lambda\operatorname{Tr}U^n\operatorname{Tr}U^m(\operatorname{Tr}U-\operatorname{Tr}U^\dagger)
\right\rangle &&\text{combine coefficients}.
\end{align}
Equating the two contracted expressions yields the stated double-trace loop equation.
\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\left\langle \frac{m}{N^2}\operatorname{Tr}U^{n+m}+\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}\operatorname{Tr}U^r\operatorname{Tr}U^{n-r}\operatorname{Tr}U^m+\frac1\lambda\operatorname{Tr}U^m(\operatorname{Tr}U^{n+1}-\operatorname{Tr}U^{n-1})\right\rangle
=\left\langle \frac{m+n}{N^2}\operatorname{Tr}U^n\operatorname{Tr}U^m+\frac1\lambda\operatorname{Tr}U^n\operatorname{Tr}U^m(\operatorname{Tr}U-\operatorname{Tr}U^\dagger)\right\rangle}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_5:
\section*{Claim}
Let $D_x:=\frac{\partial}{\partial x_\mu}\frac{\delta}{\delta\sigma_{\mu\nu}(x)}$. If a $U(N)$ Wilson loop factorizes as $W(C)=\widetilde W(C)w(C)$ under $U(N)\to SU(N)\times U(1)$, then the corresponding $SU(N)$ single-loop continuum Makeenko--Migdal equation is
\[
D_x\widetilde W(C_x)=\lambda\oint_C dy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y)\left[\widetilde W(C^{(1)}_{xy},C^{(2)}_{yx})-\frac1{N^2}\widetilde W(C)\right].
\]
\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}&\quad D_x:=\frac{\partial}{\partial x_\mu}\frac{\delta}{\delta\sigma_{\mu\nu}(x)}.\\
\text{(P2)}&\quad W(C)=\widetilde W(C)w(C).\\
\text{(P3)}&\quad W(C^{(1)}_{xy},C^{(2)}_{yx})=\widetilde W(C^{(1)}_{xy},C^{(2)}_{yx})w(C).\\
\text{(P4)}&\quad D_xW(C_x)=\lambda\oint_Cdy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y)W(C^{(1)}_{xy},C^{(2)}_{yx}).\\
\text{(P5)}&\quad D_xw(C_x)=\frac{g^2}{N}w(C)\oint_Cdy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y),\quad \lambda=g^2N.\\
\text{(P6)}&\quad D_x\text{ is linear and obeys the product rule on }\widetilde W(C)w(C).\\
\text{(P7)}&\quad w(C)\ne0.
\end{aligned}
\]
\section*{Derivation}
\begin{align}
D_xW(C_x)
&=D_x\bigl(\widetilde W(C_x)w(C_x)\bigr) &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=w(C)D_x\widetilde W(C_x)+\widetilde W(C)D_xw(C_x) &&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=w(C)D_x\widetilde W(C_x)+\frac{g^2}{N}\widetilde W(C)w(C)\oint_Cdy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y) &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=w(C)D_x\widetilde W(C_x)+\frac{\lambda}{N^2}\widetilde W(C)w(C)\oint_Cdy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y) &&\text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}
The same quantity is also
\begin{align}
D_xW(C_x)
&=\lambda\oint_Cdy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y)W(C^{(1)}_{xy},C^{(2)}_{yx}) &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=\lambda\oint_Cdy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y)\widetilde W(C^{(1)}_{xy},C^{(2)}_{yx})w(C) &&\text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}
Equating the two expressions and moving the abelian term to the right gives
\begin{align}
w(C)D_x\widetilde W(C_x)
&=\lambda w(C)\oint_Cdy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y)\widetilde W(C^{(1)}_{xy},C^{(2)}_{yx})\\
&\quad-\frac{\lambda}{N^2}\widetilde W(C)w(C)\oint_Cdy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y) &&\text{subtraction}\\
&=\lambda w(C)\oint_Cdy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y)\left[\widetilde W(C^{(1)}_{xy},C^{(2)}_{yx})-\frac1{N^2}\widetilde W(C)\right] &&\text{combine integrands}.
\end{align}
Since $w(C)\ne0$, divide by $w(C)$.
\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{D_x\widetilde W(C_x)=\lambda\oint_C dy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y)\left[\widetilde W(C^{(1)}_{xy},C^{(2)}_{yx})-\frac1{N^2}\widetilde W(C)\right]}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_7:
\section*{Claim}
If $M_{ij}:=\langle O_i^\dagger O_j\rangle$ is the Gram matrix of operators $O_i$ with respect to a positive measure, then $M$ is positive semidefinite:
\[
M\succeq0.
\]
\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}&\quad O:=\sum_i\alpha_iO_i\text{ for arbitrary complex coefficients }\alpha_i.\\
\text{(P2)}&\quad M_{ij}:=\langle O_i^\dagger O_j\rangle.\\
\text{(P3)}&\quad \langle X\rangle:=\int d\mu\,X\text{ with }d\mu\ge0.\\
\text{(P4)}&\quad O^\dagger O=|O|^2\ge0\text{ pointwise}.\\
\text{(P5)}&\quad M\succeq0\Longleftrightarrow \alpha^{*T}M\alpha\ge0\text{ for every complex vector }\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]
\section*{Derivation}
\begin{align}
\alpha^{*T}M\alpha
&=\sum_{i,j}\alpha_i^*M_{ij}\alpha_j &&\text{definition of quadratic form}\\
&=\sum_{i,j}\alpha_i^*\langle O_i^\dagger O_j\rangle\alpha_j &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=\left\langle \sum_{i,j}\alpha_i^*O_i^\dagger O_j\alpha_j\right\rangle &&\text{linearity of }\langle\cdot\rangle\\
&=\left\langle \left(\sum_i\alpha_iO_i\right)^\dagger\left(\sum_j\alpha_jO_j\right)\right\rangle &&\text{algebra of adjoints}\\
&=\langle O^\dagger O\rangle &&\text{by (P1)}\\
&=\int d\mu\,|O|^2 &&\text{by (P3) and (P4)}\\
&\ge0 &&\text{because }d\mu\ge0\text{ and }|O|^2\ge0.
\end{align}
Since the inequality holds for every $\alpha$, (P5) applies.
\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{M\succeq0}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$

core_reasoning_11:
\section*{Claim}
If rectangular Wilson loops obey the area-law form
\[
W(T,L)=\exp\{-a^2\sigma TL+r(T,L)\},
\]
then the Creutz-ratio estimator
\[
\chi(T,L):=-\log\frac{W(T,L)W(T-1,L-1)}{W(T-1,L)W(T,L-1)}
\]
satisfies
\[
\chi(T,L)=a^2\sigma-r(T,L)-r(T-1,L-1)+r(T-1,L)+r(T,L-1),
\]
and therefore equals $a^2\sigma$ when the residual term $r$ vanishes.
\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}&\quad T,L\in\mathbb{Z},\quad T\ge2,\quad L\ge2,
\quad W(T,L)>0.\\
\text{(P2)}&\quad W(T,L)=\exp\{-a^2\sigma TL+r(T,L)\}.\\
\text{(P3)}&\quad \chi(T,L):=-\log\frac{W(T,L)W(T-1,L-1)}{W(T-1,L)W(T,L-1)}.\\
\text{(P4)}&\quad \log(AB/CD)=\log A+\log B-\log C-\log D\quad\text{for }A,B,C,D>0.\\
\text{(P5)}&\quad -TL-(T-1)(L-1)+(T-1)L+T(L-1)=-1.
\end{aligned}
\]
\section*{Derivation}
Take logarithms of the area-law form:
\begin{align}
\log W(T,L)&=-a^2\sigma TL+r(T,L) &&\text{by (P2)}\\
\log W(T-1,L-1)&=-a^2\sigma (T-1)(L-1)+r(T-1,L-1) &&\text{by (P2)}\\
\log W(T-1,L)&=-a^2\sigma (T-1)L+r(T-1,L) &&\text{by (P2)}\\
\log W(T,L-1)&=-a^2\sigma T(L-1)+r(T,L-1) &&\text{by (P2)}.
\end{align}
Substitute these four identities into the Creutz ratio:
\begin{align}
\chi(T,L)
&=-\log\frac{W(T,L)W(T-1,L-1)}{W(T-1,L)W(T,L-1)} &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=-\bigl[\log W(T,L)+\log W(T-1,L-1)-\log W(T-1,L)-\log W(T,L-1)\bigr] &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=-\bigl[-a^2\sigma TL+r(T,L)-a^2\sigma (T-1)(L-1)+r(T-1,L-1)\\
&\quad\quad{}+a^2\sigma (T-1)L-r(T-1,L)+a^2\sigma T(L-1)-r(T,L-1)\bigr] &&\text{substitute the logarithms}\\
&=-a^2\sigma\bigl[-TL-(T-1)(L-1)+(T-1)L+T(L-1)\bigr]\\
&\quad{}-r(T,L)-r(T-1,L-1)+r(T-1,L)+r(T,L-1) &&\text{collect }\sigma\text{ and }r\text{ terms}\\
&=a^2\sigma-r(T,L)-r(T-1,L-1)+r(T-1,L)+r(T,L-1) &&\text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}
If $r(A,B)=0$ for the four rectangles appearing above, then the same expression gives $\chi(T,L)=a^2\sigma$.
\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\chi(T,L)=a^2\sigma-r(T,L)-r(T-1,L-1)+r(T-1,L)+r(T,L-1)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
